content:
Short answer: you can sign up and list yourself on Collabstr for free, but it is not commission-free. Collabstr takes 15% of what you earn on each order. Here is how the fees work on both sides, how you get paid, and which platforms let you keep more.

Disclosure: Newcollab is also a platform for UGC creators. We only state what the other platforms publish on their own pricing, FAQ and help pages, link the source for each fact, and describe our own product in the same way. We checked every page in November 2026; fees change, so confirm on the platform before you sign up.

What Collabstr charges creators

Collabstr's pricing page says creators pay "a separate 15% fee on their payout", and its creator page says there is no up-front cost to join. The 15% is only taken when you complete an order, so an empty profile costs nothing.

Order priceCollabstr fee (15%)You receive
$100$15$85
$200$30$170
$500$75$425

Tip: if you want to take home a set amount, divide it by 0.85 to get your list price. To take home $150 per video, list it at about $177.

What brands pay (and why it does not reduce your pay)

Brands pay Collabstr separately. The pricing page lists a free brand plan and paid plans (Pro $249 a month, Premium $333 a month, billed annually, with an Enterprise tier above that), plus a fee on each hire: 10% on Free and Pro, 5% on Premium. That fee is added to what the brand pays. It does not come out of your 15%-reduced payout.

How Collabstr payouts work

  • The brand pays up front and Collabstr holds the money until the order is approved or completed, then releases it.
  • Payouts go through Collabstr's payout partner, with options such as PayPal, Venmo and Cash App, depending on your country.
  • Collabstr does not publish a fixed number of days from approval to payout.

Who can join Collabstr

Collabstr reviews every profile before it shows up in the marketplace. It does not publish a follower minimum, and it accepts Instagram, TikTok, YouTube and UGC creators. You set fixed-price packages that brands buy, and brands can also invite you to campaigns.

Is Collabstr worth it for small creators?

It can be, if brands find and buy your packages. The fee is the trade-off for the traffic Collabstr brings. The risk for new creators is waiting on inbound orders that never come. Most UGC creators who get steady work combine one or two platforms with pitching brands directly, where nobody takes a cut.

When a brand hires you from your own pitch, there is no platform fee at all.
